written: 2026-09-05, from the fixture sources, BEFORE ADR-A020 was written and BEFORE any code changed
question: When M13's B4 boundary fires, does the existing unresolved-member flag REMAIN alongside the fetched surface, or is it REPLACED by it?
note_on_order: The milestone asks for ADR-A020 first. This key was written first because the ADR must record the answer to the question above, and the answer is what the key establishes. Both precede implementation.

the_two_alternatives.RETAIN: the unresolved-reference flag stays AND the class surface is fetched — two outcomes for one assertion, the shape the caller-truncation case already uses
the_two_alternatives.REPLACE: the surface is fetched INSTEAD of the flag — the reference is treated as resolved

decided_by: row H. `Package::activatte` satisfies all three B4 conditions identically to `Package::create` — placeable, project source, member unresolved — and ADR-A016 proved that no fact available to the tool separates them. Under REPLACE the typo silently becomes 'here is the model surface' with no warning attached, which is exactly M0 risk R1 and the silent omission P10 forbids. A rule that cannot tell a typo from a method must not make a decision that depends on telling them apart.
cost_of_retain: an Eloquent member reference produces two items: a flag whose statement ADR-A016 already records as arguably false, and a surface. That duplication is the price of keeping the typo visible, and it is recorded rather than hidden.

rows.expected: Package SURFACE fetched (fillable, casts, scopeActive) AND the existing flag retained
rows.why: Experiment 1's earned move. The flag stays for the reason row H gives.

rows.expected: surface + flag; no ADDITIONAL surface beyond A's
rows.why: One surface per class however many members are referenced.

rows.expected: surface + flag; still no additional surface

rows.why: A second, independent model — the result must not come from one lucky class.

rows.expected: the `create` member slice ONLY — no surface, no flag; byte-identical to today
rows.why: THE TRAP. `create` is Eloquent's most recognisable name on an ordinary final class. B4's third condition excludes it because the member resolves — never because of the name. Fetching `__construct` and `all` too would be a new over-fetch.

rows.expected: exactly ONE flagged item, no surface, no duplicate flag; byte-identical to today
rows.why: B4's first condition excludes it. A surface here is impossible and a second flag would be a new false positive.

rows.expected: no item at all — M3's framework-known settlement, unchanged; no project surface; no vendor source in the bundle

rows.conditions: placeable + project + member unresolved — IDENTICAL to B
rows.expected: the flag MUST remain. The Package surface is already present from A/B/C and is not duplicated for this reference.
rows.why: THE DECIDING ROW. Indistinguishable from B by any available fact (ADR-A016). If B4 replaced the flag, this typo would be reported as satisfied context. It must not be.

rows.reference: App\Models\Widget via new/param/return; App\Models\Invoice via `?Invoice` AND `Invoice::create`
rows.expected: Widget surface fetched exactly once, as today. Invoice surface fetched exactly ONCE despite being reached two ways — no duplicate surface.
rows.why: Invoice is the duplicate guard: a class referenced both as a bare type and through an unresolved member must yield one surface, not two.

rows.reference: docblock, @see, line comment, string literals, Package::class
rows.expected: ZERO items from any of them
bundle_version 1, schema, assertion kinds, premises, levers, provenance shape, ItemPriority bands and token accounting UNCHANGED; no new port; no second source file opened beyond the located one
rows.why: M14 adds a fallback inside an existing resolution path and nothing else.
